records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF MINES (SHRI DINSHA PATEL)<br/><br/>(a) to (c): The Government has amended the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) (MMDR) Act, 1957 in the year 2010 to provide  for allocation of blocks for coal minerals through auction by competitive bidding. <br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Suicide by Bt. Cotton farmers
records.name: Sukhendu Sekhar Ray
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether an internal advisory dated 9 January, 2012 sent by the Ministry to cotton growing States affirms that suicide by Bt. Cotton farmers were severe in 2011-12;<br/><br/>(b)	 if so, the assessment of Indian Agricultural Science with regard to shifting of cotton farmers to Bt. Cotton and the resultant adverse effect thereof;<br/><br/>(c) 	whether Government is aware of a documentary film titled ''Bitter Seeds'' on suicide by Bt. Cotton farmers in India which bagged 18 international film awards; and<br/><br/>(d) 	if so, how Government reacts to such international repercussions and commit to nation to stop forthwith such human tragedies?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES  <br/><br/>(SHRI  TARIQ  ANWAR)<br/><br/><br/>(a):	No, Sir.<br/><br/>(b):	Question does not arise.<br/><br/>(c):	As per the information furnished by the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, Film Division has not produced any Documentary Film regarding suicide by Bt. Cotton farmers.  However, US-based film maker Shri Micha Peled has produced a documentary film titled “Bitter Seeds”.<br/><br/>(d):	The Government lays maximum emphasis in assessing and minimizing the problems being faced by the farmers in cultivation of Crops.  The Scientists of State Agriculture Universities, Indian Council of Agricultural Research and Officials of the States Directorate of Agriculture constantly interact with the farmers to assess their problems and take appropriate steps/develop technologies to reduce their miseries/tragedies, if any. <br/><br/>	Cultivation of Bt. Cotton has resulted in increase in income of the farmers and in improving their standard of living.  The yield of cotton has increased from 190 kg lint per ha to 491 kg lint per ha.  Area under Bt. Cotton has increased by more than 90% of the total cotton area in the country.  Reasons for suicide by farmers as reported by the State Governments, are manifold which, inter-alia includes indebtedness, socio-economic and personal reasons, crop failure & drought. There seems to be no evidence of direct relationship between Bt. Cotton and farmers’ suicides. <br/><br/>********<br/>

records.qtitle: Introduction of FDI in multi brand retail trade
records.name: Sukhendu Sekhar Ray
records.qn_text: (a)	whether Government proposes to introduce Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) in multi-brand retail trade in India;<br/>(b)	if so, whether any in-depth study has been done on its possible socio-economic impact, once the decision is implemented;<br/>(c)	if so, the details thereof;<br/>(d)	if not, the reasons for taking the decision, if any, for introduction of FDI in multi-brand retail trade in the country; and <br/>(e)	how many Indians are engaged in retail trade in our country and whether there would be uneven and unwarranted competition among equals with unequals once decision, if any, for FDI in multi-brand retail trade is taken in India?
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY <br/>(SHRI ANAND SHARMA)<br/><br/><br/>(a)	to (e):    A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.	<br/><br/>*******   <br/> <br/><br/>STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN  REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION    NO. 351 FOR ANSWER ON WEDNESDAY, THE 5TH SEPTEMBER, 2012 ON ‘INTRODUCTION OF FDI IN MULTI-BRAND RETAIL TRADE’.<br/><br/><br/><br/>(a): 	Government has approved a proposal to permit FDI, up to 51%, under the Government approval route, in multi-brand retail trading, subject to specified conditions. The decision has been suspended, in order to evolve a broader consensus among various stakeholders.<br/>(b): 	The Government had instituted a study, on the subject of “Impact of Organized Retailing on the Unorganized Sector”, through the Indian Council for Research on International Economic Relations (ICRIER), which was submitted to Government in 2008.<br/>(c): 	Main findings of the ICRIER study are annexed.<br/>(d):	The ICRIER study indicates significant benefits for various stakeholders, such as consumers, farmers and manufacturers, arising as a result of the growth of organized retail. Discussions have been held with representatives of consumer associations/organizations, Micro & Small Industry Associations, farmers’ associations and representatives of food processing industry and industry associations. While views for and against FDI in multi-brand retail trading were expressed, the discussions generally indicate support for the policy, subject to the introduction of adequate safeguards.<br/>(e):	NSSO data indicates that retail trade employed 33 million persons in 2007-08. The ICRIER study noted that both unorganized and organized retail not only coexist but also grow substantially in size, as a result of the growth of organized retail. Further, there was no evidence of a decline in overall employment in the unorganized sector as a result of the entry of organized retailers in the long-run. The ICRIER study has estimated substantial growth for both the organized and unorganized retail sectors. Employment in the retail sector, both organized and unorganized, is also expected to grow significantly, in line with the growth of the retail sector.<br/><br/>*******

records.qtitle: Expansion of trade areas with countries having trade relations
records.name: Sukhendu Sekhar Ray
records.qn_text: <br/>a)	whether Government have any proposal under consideration to add new areas of trade with countries having trade relations with India;<br/><br/>b)	if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>c)	the total revenue likely to be generated from expansion of such trade areas; and<br/><br/>d)	what action Government has initiated to minimize the trade deficit during the current financial year?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY<br/>(SHRI JYOTIRADITYA M. SCINDIA)<br/><br/>(a)& (b) :   It is a constant endeavor of the Government to enhance trade with our trade partners  for mutual benefit.  In this context, India has taken various initiatives like Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreements (CECA), Free Trade Agreements (FTA) Preferential Trade Agreements (PTA)  etc. with various countries.   Some of the FTAs/PTAs are – Agreement on South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA), India-Singapore Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement (CECA), India-South Korea Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA),  India-Japan Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (ECPA), India- Malaysia Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement (CECA),  India-ASEAN Trade in Goods Agreement,  Asia Pacific  Trade Agreement (APTA), India-MERCOCUR (PTA) etc..<br/><br/>(c)     :   It is not feasible to estimate total revenue to be generated from such expansion.<br/><br/>(d)  :  The Government reviews performance of export sectors at regular intervals and takes remedial measures for providing incentives whenever needed to boost export  which, in turn, reduce trade  deficit.   In the Annual Supplement (2012-13) to  the Foreign Trade Policy (2009-14), a number of incentives have been announced by the Government which  include extension of  2% interest subvention scheme to  toys, sports goods, processed agricultural products and readymade garments; extension of zero duty EPCG Scheme upto  31st March, 2013; enlarging the  scope of EPCG Scheme; relief from export obligations under EPCG Scheme to some sectors; allowance of 10% of  Status Holders Incentive Scrip to import components and spares of Capital goods imported earlier etc.<br/><br/>                                                              *****************<br/>

records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COAL<br/> (SHRI PRATIK PRAKASHBAPU PATIL)<br/><br/>(a):  Details are given at Annexure.<br/><br/>(b): The information is being collected and would be laid on the table of the House.<br/><br/>(c): As the price of coal is de-regulated, the Coal India Limited (CIL) decides the same keeping in view its commercial interest.<br/><br/>(d): Coal blocks are allocated for specified end uses for captive consumption. records.name: Sukhendu Sekhar Ray
records.qn_text: (a)	whether some of the States have petitioned to Government for allotment of special funds or for enhancement of funds during the current financial year;<br/>(b)	whether Government has decided to sanction special funds or enhanced allotment of funds to different States for the current financial year;<br/>(c)	if so, the details thereof along with reasons, State-wise; and <br/>(d)	if not, the reasons thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: The Minister of Finance<br/>SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM<br/><br/>(a) to (d): 	A Statement is laid on the table of the House.<br/><br/><br/> <br/>Statement referred to in reply to Rajya Sabha Starred Question No.162 for answer on 23.08.2012.<br/><br/>(a) to (d): 		Requests are received from States from time to time, for financial assistance for various purposes, as also for enhancement of financial assistance. Requests received from States during the current financial year for Plan assistance have largely been factored in at the time of finalization of Annual State Plans in the Planning Commission after discussion with Chief Ministers of the States on an assessment of inter-state and inter-sectoral Plan priorities within the overall resource availability at the Central and State level. The aggregate Plan size of the States has increased from Rs. 4,65,434 crore in 2011-12 to Rs. 5,53,801 crore  in 2012-13 representing an increase of about 19%. Approved outlay for Central Assistance to the State Plans, including Special Plan Assistance, Special Central Assistance to the Special Category States, has increased from Rs.1,02,050.73 crore in 2011-12 to Rs. 1,24,042.49 crore in 2012-13, an increase of about 21%.  State-wise details are at Annex-I and II respectively.<br/><br/>	Apart from the foregoing, development efforts in States are also supported through Assistance for Central and Centrally Sponsored Schemes. The total provision of Central Assistance increased from Rs.1,52,859 crore in 2011-12(RE) to Rs.1,78,906 crore in 2012-13(BE). <br/>

records.qtitle: Measures for reducing infant mortality rate
records.name: Sukhendu Sekhar Ray
records.qn_text: (a) whether India ranks top among the 121 nations of the world in the field of<br/>underweight children below the age of five years;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the steps Government has taken so far to improve the health of the<br/>children in the country;<br/><br/>(c) whether the child mortality rate is 47.57 per thousand live births;<br/><br/>(d) whether it is also a fact that India stood at 51st position among 220 countries<br/>so far as the child mortality rate is concerned; and<br/><br/>(e) if so, the reasons for such alarming situation and the remedial measures<br/>adopted by Government in this regard to minimise the child mortality rate?<br/>
records.ans_text: (a) As per World Health Statistics report 2012, India stands 2nd rank in the field of underweight children below the age of five years.<br/>(b) Malnutrition is multidimensional and intergenerational and requires interventions through various Ministries to address its many underlying causes in different stages of the life cycle. <br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>Under NRHM, the remedial steps taken are as follows: <br/>?	Promotion of appropriate infant and young child feeding practices that include early initiation of breastfeeding and exclusive breastfeeding till 6 months of age.<br/>?	Management of malnutrition and common neonatal and childhood illnesses at community and facility level by training service providers in IMNCI (Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illnesses) training.<br/>?	Treatment of children with severe acute malnutrition at special units called the Nutrition Rehabilitation Centres (NRCs), set up at public health facilities. Presently 564 such centres are functional all over the country.<br/>?	Specific program to prevent and combat micronutrient deficiencies of Vitamin A and Iron & Folic Acid.  Vitamin A supplementation for children till the age of 5 years and Iron & Folic Acid supplementation for children 6 to 60 months. <br/>?	Village Health and Nutrition Days and Mother and Child Protection Card are the joint initiative of the Ministries of Health & Family welfare and the Ministry of Woman and Child for addressing the nutrition concerns in children, pregnant women and lactating mothers.<br/>?	Nutrition Education on VHNDs (Village Health and Nutrition Days) to increase the awareness and bring about desired changes in the dietary practices including the promotion of breastfeeding.<br/>?	Growth monitoring of children up to three years  by promoting use of Mother and Child Protection card. <br/>(c)No.   As per office of Registrar General of India, SRS 2010 report, India has Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) of  47 per 1000 live births.<br/>(d) As per World Health Statistics report 2012, India stands 47th rank of infant mortality rate in the world.<br/>(e):  The causes of infant deaths in India 2001-03 as given by the Registrar General of India, Ministry of Home Affairs, are  Perinatal conditions (46%), Respiratory infections (22%), Diarrhoeal disease (10%), Other infectious and parasitic diseases (8%) and Congenital anomalies (3.1%).  Factors contributing to above causes are home delivery by unskilled persons, lack of essential new born care for asphyxia and hypothermia , poor child care practices, lack of early detection of sick newborn, inadequate/delayed referral mechanisms, inadequate infrastructure at health care facilities for specialized care of sick newborn etc.<br/><br/>The following interventions under RCH progamme of NRHM are being implemented.<br/><br/>1)	Prevention and treatment of Anaemia by supplementation with Iron and Folic Acid tablets during pregnancy and lactation. <br/>2)	Name Based Tracking of Pregnant Women to ensure complete antenatal, intranatal and postnatal care<br/>3)	Operationalizing Community Health Centers as First Referral Units (FRUs) and Primary Health Centers (24X7) for round the clock maternal care services. )<br/>4)	Promotion of Institutional Delivery through Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) and Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK): Promoting Institutional delivery to ensure skilled birth attendance is key to reducing both maternal and neo-natal mortality. <br/>5)	Strengthening Facility based newborn care: Newborn care corners (NBCC) are being set up at all health facilities where deliveries take place; Special New Born Care Units (SNCUs) and New Born Stabilization Units (NBSUs) are also being set up at appropriate facilities for the care of sick newborn including preterm babies.<br/>6)	Home Based Newborn Care (HBNC):  Home based newborn care through ASHA has been initiated to improve new born practices at the community level and early detection and referral of sick new born babies<br/>7)	Capacity building of health care providers: Various trainings are being conducted under National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) to build and upgrade the skills of health care providers in basic and comprehensive obstetric care of mother during pregnancy, delivery and essential newborn care.<br/>8)	Adolescent Reproductive Sexual Health Programme (ARSH)– Specially  for adolescents to have better access to family planning, prevention of Sexually transmitted Infections, Provision of counselling and peer education.<br/>

records.qtitle: Market share of MTNL and BSNL
records.name: Sukhendu Sekhar Ray
records.qn_text: (a) 	the market share of MTNL and BSNL in the mobile market in the country; <br/><br/>(b) 	whether it is a fact that MTNL and BSNL have been affected adversely by the fierce competition in the mobile market;<br/><br/>(c) 	if so, the details thereof; and<br/><br/>(d) 	the measures being taken by Government to revive marketability of the two giant telecommunication companies?
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY ( SHRI MILIND DEORA)<br/><br/>(a) 	The market share of Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) and Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Limited (MTNL) in wireless segment for the last three years and current year (as on 30.06.2012) is given below:<br/><br/> <pre>        <br/>Date	   Wireless Market Share %<br/>	          BSNL    MTNL<br/>31.03.2010	11.88	9.30<br/>31.03.2011	11.32	7.43<br/>31.03.2012	10.71	7.40<br/>30.06.2012	10.55	7.09<br/>                                                        </pre>                       <br/><br/>(b)&(c)	BSNL  and MTNL have been affected adversely by the fierce competition in the mobile market. The main reasons for declining mobile market share of BSNL and MTNL are as follows:<br/><br/>•	Entry of new operators and consequent price war with entry of new operators <br/>•	Lack of effective marketing<br/>•	Poor customer service<br/><br/>In addition, BSNL’s market share declined also due to delay in augmentation of capacity of Global System for Mobile communication (GSM) equipment.<br/>Contd…2/-<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>-2-<br/><br/>(d) 	Department of Telecommunications (DoT) reviews the performance of BSNL and MTNL periodically. To ensure the growth in the hyper-competitive mobile industry, some steps have been taken by BSNL and MTNL which are as follows:<br/><br/>BSNL<br/>	<br/>•	Strengthening of sales and distribution channel of mobile through Project Vijay.<br/>•	Augmentation of capacity in Phase-VII by 15 Million.<br/>•	Weekly meeting with Franchisees / Retailers and Sales teams of BSNL at district level.<br/>•	Fixing of target to sales team and ensuring delivery of material. <br/>•	Fixing and monitoring retailer manager wise target. <br/>•	Special camp to interact with customer willing to port out for their retention by sorting out their problems. <br/>•	Opening new sales channels in rural areas through agreement with Postal department to increase rural reach.<br/>•	Aggressively push smart devices bundled with 3G Data plans as well as wireless broadband with 3G data cards.<br/>•	Sustained Focus on Value Added Services catering to various segments of the society.<br/>•	Monitoring of Quality of Service (QoS) parameters to adhere to the benchmarks stipulated by Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI).<br/>		<br/>MTNL <br/>•	MTNL is reviewing its tariff for various products and services so as to make them customer friendly and to suit various segments of the society.<br/>•	MTNL has taken a lot of measures to facilitate easy payment of telephone bills to meet the requirement of all segment of society.<br/>•	Loyalty scheme & special care of corporate customers.<br/>•	MTNL is operating call centre/help lines for the customers to book their grievances. <br/>•	Online booking of different services and complaints for landline and mobile are now available.<br/>•	MTNL is having Sanchar Haats in Delhi and Customer Service Centers (CSCs) at Mumbai, where customer can get various services like registration for new service, duplicate bills of cellular connection, bill payment, VCC cards etc. <br/><br/>In addition, the National Telecom Policy (NTP- 2012) inter-alia envisages following role of Public Sector Units, including BSNL and  MTNL:<br/>•	To recognise the strategic importance of Telecom PSUs in nurturing/ enhancing Government’s intervention capabilities in matters of national security or international importance, including execution of bilateral projects funded by Government of India.<br/><br/>•	To encourage Public Sector Units under the DoT to identify and exploit strategic and operational synergies so that they play a significant role in service provision, infrastructure creation, and manufacturing.<br/><br/>•	To exploit individual strengths of organisations under DoT/Department of Information Technology (DIT) to their mutual benefit for ensuring these organisations to effectively flourish in the competitive telecom market while adequately supporting the security needs of the nation. Efforts will be made for according preferential treatment for procurement of products and services rendered by individual organisations.<br/>************

records.qtitle: Real GDP Growth rate in India
records.name: Sukhendu Sekhar Ray
records.qn_text: (a)whether it is a fact that GDP real growth rate in India which was between 6.2 per cent and 7.4 <br/>per cent during 2004 to 2009 rose to 9 per cent in 2010-11, but reached its lowest ebb during the    <br/>first quarter of current year, estimated at 5.3 per cent;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the reasons therefor;<br/><br/>(c) if so, the action initiated by Government for enhancement of growth rate;<br/><br/>(d) whether it is a fact that exchange rate of  one US dollar was  Rs.48.40 in 2009, came down to Rs.  <br/>45.72 in 2010, further reduced to Rs.44.64 in 2011 and has at present reached on all time high  <br/>ranging between Rs. 55.42 and 54.30; and<br/><br/>(e)if so, the reasons therefor and the action taken by Government to address the problem?  <br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE<br/>(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA)<br/><br/>(a) The details of the growth rate of India’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) at Factor Cost at Constant (2004-05) prices are given in the Table below: <br/>------------------------------------------------------<br/>Table: Annual Growth Rate of Gross Domestic Product at Factor Cost at Constant (2004-05) Prices<br/>------------------------------------------------------<br/>      2003  2004  2005 2006 2007 2008 2009 2010  2011  <br/>       -04   -05   -06  -07  -08  -09  -10  -11   -12<br/>------------------------------------------------------<br/>Total  8.1   7.0   9.5	9.6  9.3  6.7  8.4  8.4	  6.5<br/>Gross <br/>Domestic <br/>Product <br/>at <br/>Factor cost<br/>----------------------------------------------------- <br/>Source: CSO.<br/><br/>As per the quarterly data released by the Central Statistics Office (CSO), India’s growth rate was 5.3 per cent in the fourth quarter of the financial year 2011-12. This growth has been the lowest since the fourth quarter of the financial year 2008-09, when the growth rate was 3.5 per cent. <br/><br/>(b) The slowdown in the growth of the economy is mainly on account of the slowdown in the industrial sector and lower growth registered in the agriculture sector. This reduction in the growth rate is attributable to both domestic and global factors. Global factors include, in particular, the crisis in the euro-zone and the near-recessionary conditions prevailing in Europe; sluggish growth in several industrialized economies; hardening of international prices of crude oil, etc. Among domestic factors, the tightening of monetary policy in order to control inflation resulted in the slowing down of investment and growth, particularly in the industrial sector.<br/><br/>(c)  The action plan of the Government to revive the economy, inter alia, includes better access to finance for manufacturing sector, fast tracking of large investment projects in the areas of power, petroleum and gas, roads, coal, etc., use of buffer stocks to moderate food inflation, strengthening of financial and banking sector, reducing the volatility of exchange rate, etc. Certain specific measures taken by the Government to achieve the growth target, inter alia, include enhancing the level of investment for agriculture sector including irrigation projects, promoting Micro Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME) sector by way of higher allocation of funds, enhancing investment in the infrastructure sector focusing on Public Private Partnerships, a number of legislative measures to develop the financial sector and introduction of a new National Manufacturing Policy, etc. The fiscal policy as enunciated in the Budget 2012-13 aims at reducing the fiscal deficit from 5.8 per cent in 2011-12 to 5.1 per cent in 2012-13, by restricting the expenditure on subsidies to under 2 per cent of GDP. This would be facilitated by the move towards nutrient based subsidy in fertilizers and the use of unique identity based ‘Aadhaar’ system for rationalizing subsidies. Steps have been taken to expedite the passage of Direct Tax Code Bill and evolving a consensus among stake holders in implementation of goods and services tax.  <br/><br/>(d)  The exchange rate of Indian Rupee against US dollar at the end of March of 2009, 2010, 2011 and 2012 as well as for the financial year 2012-13 so far (as on August 10, 2012) is given in the Table below: <br/><br/>Table : Exchange Rate of the Indian Rupee against the US Dollar <br/><br/>As at end-March	            Rupees per US Dollar<br/><br/>2009	                          50.95<br/>2010	                          45.13<br/>2011	                          44.65<br/><br/>2012<br/>As at end-	<br/>March	                          51.16<br/>April	                          52.52<br/>May	                          56.01<br/>June	                          56.31<br/>July	                          55.81<br/>August  10, 2012	          55.34<br/><br/>Source; Reserve Bank of India (RBI).<br/><br/>(e) The reason for the decline of rupee against US dollar is the supply-demand imbalance in the domestic foreign exchange market. This is due to widening of trade and current account deficit and volatility in portfolio flows on account of escalation in euro zone crisis and strengthening of US dollar in the international market due to the safe haven status of US Treasuries. The Government of India and the Reserve Bank of India have taken a number of steps to facilitate capital inflows and boost exports in order to augment supply of foreign exchange to stem the decline in the exchange rate value of the Rupee. Recent measures taken, inter alia, include hike in FII investment in debt securities (both corporate and Government securities), enhancing all-in-cost ceiling for external sector borrowings  (ECBs)  between 3-5 year maturity, higher interest rate ceiling for foreign currency Non-resident deposits  and deregulation of interest rates on rupee denominated NRI deposits. The manufacturing and infrastructure sector companies can now avail of external sector borrowing up to a ceiling of US$ 10 billion for repayment of outstanding rupee loans towards capital expenditure. Besides, under the Annual Supplement 2012-13 to Foreign Trade Policy 2009-14, the Government has announced initiatives to boost exports to about US$ 360 billion in 2012-13.  <br/>                           *****<br/>

records.qtitle: Restructuring of NPAs of nationalised banks
records.name: Sukhendu Sekhar Ray
records.qn_text: (a)  	the quantum of Non-Performing Assets (NPAs) accumulated by the nationalised banks as on 31 December, 2011 and the quantum of NPAs which has been written off during the period 2010-11;<br/><br/>(b)  	the number of borrowers declared as wilful defaulters as per the guidelines of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) during 2010-11; and<br/><br/>(c)	the quantum of restructured loans in the nationalised banks during 2010-11?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF FINANCE<br/>SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE)<br/><br/>(a): 	The Gross Non-Performing Assets (NPAs) of Nationalised Banks as on 31st December, 2011 is Rs 59,397 Crore and the quantum of NPAs written off by such banks during the period 2010-11 is Rs. 12,043.21 crore. The number of wilful defaulters, as per guidelines issued by RBI, in respect of Nationalized Banks as on March 31, 2011 is 716. <br/><br/>(c): 	The loans amounting to Rs. 46,934.58 crore have been restructured in the Nationalized Banks during the year 2010-11 (as on 31.03.2011).<br/> <br/>

records.qtitle: Bailout package for Debt Stressed States
records.name: Sukhendu Sekhar Ray
records.qn_text: (a) whether West Bengal falls within the category of ''Debt Stressed State; along with Kerala and Punjab as per F. No. 4(5)/FRU/2004, issued by Government of India, Ministry of Finance, Department of Economic Affairs on 4th August 2004; <br/><br/>(b) if so, whether the Union Government has taken any steps to bailout these Debt Stressed States; <br/><br/>(c)  if so, the details thereof; and<br/><br/>(d)  if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE<br/>(SHRI  NAMO  NARAIN MEENA)<br/> (a) Vide office memorandum no. 4(5) /FRU/2004 dated 4th August, 2004, States were advised to obtain concurrence of the Department of Expenditure before availing loan from external agencies. A debt stressed State was defined as one whose ratio of consolidated debt and liabilities to total revenue receipts exceeded 300% (200% in case of special category states).<br/>Subsequently, vide office memorandum no. 4(5)/FRU/2004 dated 24th October, 2005, States were asked to obtain concurrence of the Department of Expenditure before availing external assistance for structural adjustment loans as also for projects. A debt stressed State was defined as one with interest payments to total revenue receipts ratio higher than 20 percent. A tentative indicative list of debt-stressed States, based on the States’ 2004-05 (RE), was annexed to this office memorandum, in which Kerala, Punjab and West Bengal were three of the eleven States included.<br/><br/>(b) to (d): In accordance with the recommendations of the Twelfth Finance Commission (TFC), whose award period was 2005-10, the following public debt and interest relief measures have been extended to the States, upon their enactment of the prescribed Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Acts (FRBMA):<br/><br/>i. Central loans from Ministry of Finance contracted till 31.3.2004 and outstanding as on 31.3.2005, amounting to Rs.113601.14 crore, were consolidated for a fresh tenure of twenty years from 1.4.2005 at an interest rate of 7.5% per annum, for 26 States that had enacted their FRBMAs.<br/>ii. Debts owed to the Ministry of Finance, amounting to Rs.19725.81 crore have been waived for States based on their fiscal performance during TFC’s award period.<br/>In accordance with the recommendations of the Thirteenth Finance Commission, the following public debt and interest relief measures have been extended to the States, upon their enactment/amendment of the prescribed FRBMA:<br/><br/>i.	Central loans from Ministry of Finance contracted till 31.3.2004 and outstanding as on 31.3.2010, amounting to Rs.113.45 crore and Rs.8633.50 crore in respect of the two States, Sikkim and West Bengal respectively, which enacted their FRBMAs in 2010-11, were consolidated for a fresh tenure of twenty years from 1.4.2010 at an interest rate of 7.5% per annum.<br/>ii.	A decision to write-off loans for Centrally Sponsored Schemes/Central Plan Schemes (raised from ministries other than Ministry of Finance) outstanding at the end of 31.3.2010 has been taken. Central loans amounting to Rs.2050 crore have been written off so far.<br/>iii.	Loans contracted by States from the National Small Savings Fund till 2006-07, and outstanding at the end of year preceding the year of amendment/enactment of FRBMA, have been reset at 9% interest rate from the date of amendment/enactment of the FRBMA. Interest relief benefit of Rs.36.08 crore for 2010-11 and Rs.1060.21 crore for 2011-12 has been extended to the States so far.

records.qtitle: Shifting of LCS from Mahadipur
records.name: Sukhendu Sekhar Ray
records.qn_text: SHIFTING OF LCS FROM MAHADIPUR<br/><br/>3477. SHRI SUKHENDU SEKHAR ROY:<br/><br/>Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:<br/><br/><br/>a)	Whether the Union Government is considering any proposal to shift the Land Customs Station (LCS) from Mahadipur in the district of Malda, West Bengal Keeping in view the rampant air pollution caused due to plying of hundreds of goods vehicles at Indo-Bangladesh Border resulting to degradation and spoliation of the 17 Ancient Monuments of Gaur dynasty in the vicinity being maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI);<br/><br/>b)	If, so, the details thereof; and <br/><br/>c)	If not, the reasons thereof?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE<br/>(SHRI S.S.PALANIMANICKAM)<br/><br/>a)	No Sir. There is no proposal or request for shifting of Mahadipur Land Customs Station, West Bengal to any other location.<br/> 		<br/>b)	Nil, in view of above.<br/><br/>c)	Archeological Survey of India, the nodal agency in this connection, has informed that there are seventeen monuments under the protection of Archeological Survey of India in Gaur, District of Malda in West Bengal and that as on date, there is no definite evidence of damage to them from air pollution due to the movement of vehicular traffic.<br/><br/>*****

records.qtitle: Restructuring of loans of West Bengal
records.name: Sukhendu Sekhar Ray
records.qn_text: (a)	Whether the State Government of West Bengal has inherited and is carrying over a debt burden worth  Rs.12 lakh crores from previous Government in the State;<br/>(b)	if so, whether the Chief Minister of West Bengal has requested the Union Government to put a moratorium on repayment of interest for three years in the form of grant and a total restructuring of  the loan amount;<br/>(c)	if so, whether such request is under consideration of the Union Government;<br/>(d)	if so, the details thereof; and<br/>(e)	if not, the reasons therefor?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE<br/>(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA)<br/><br/>(a)	No, Sir. As per the Finance Accounts of the State Government of West Bengal for the year 2010-11, the total public debt and other liabilities of the State stood at Rs.1,87,387 Crore as on 31st March 2011. <br/><br/>(b)	 to (e) A letter has been received from the State Government of West Bengal requesting an interest and repayment moratorium on the outstanding debt of the State (in the form of   an annual grant) for a period of three consecutive years, which is under examination. <br/><br/>In accordance with the recommendations of Thirteenth Finance Commission (FC-XIII), for its award period 2010-15, the following public debt and interest relief measures have already been extended to the State of West Bengal: <br/><br/>i.	Central loans (from Ministry of Finance) outstanding on 31st March 2010, amounting to Rs.8633.50 crore have been consolidated for a fresh tenure of 20 years at an interest rate of 7.5% p.a. with effect from 1st April, 2010<br/>ii.	Central loans for Central Sector Schemes/Central Plan Schemes (other than Ministry of Finance) outstanding as at the end of 2009-10, amounting to Rs.110.55 crore have been written off in March 2012. <br/>iii.	The loans contracted by West Bengal from the National Small Savings Fund till 2006-07 and outstanding at the end of year preceding the year of enactment of Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act (FRBMA), have been reset at 9% interest rate from the date of enactment of the FRBMA, i.e. 7-2-2011. An interest relief of Rs.3.81 crore has been extended for 2010-11 and Rs.269.32 crore for 2011-12. <br/>

records.qtitle: Protection of ancient site of Gaur in West Bengal from pollution
records.name: Sukhendu Sekhar Ray
records.qn_text: <br/>(a)	whether Government is aware that due to emission of carbon monoxide, movement of hundreds of trucks carrying export goods, through the land customs station at Mahadipur, P.S. Englishbazar, Distt. Malda in West Bengal, the ancient monuments and archaeological site of Gaur in the vicinity, which was the capital of Bengal for over 600 years, are being subjected to unabated pollution and damage of those monuments being maintained by Archaeological Survey of India (ASI);<br/>(b)	if so, what remedial measures have been adopted by Government; and <br/>(c)	if not, the reasons therefor?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: <br/><br/>(a) to (c)	There are seventeen monuments under the protection of Archaeological Survey of India in Gaur, District Malda in West Bengal.  As on date, there is no definite evidence of damage from air pollution due to the movement of vehicular traffic.<br/>	<br/>	<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Circuit Bench of Calcutta High Court
records.name: Sukhendu Sekhar Ray
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government is aware that in spite of the long standing<br/>demand of the people of North Bengal and even though all<br/>infrastructure is ready for running of a Circuit Bench of Calcutta<br/>High Court, the same has not yet started functioning;<br/>(b) if so, by when the said Circuit Bench would start functioning in<br/>Jalpaiguri district of West Bengal; and<br/>(c) if the Circuit Bench could not be started in near future, the<br/>reasons therefor?
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>MINISTER OF LAW AND JUSTICE<br/>(SHRI SALMAN KHURSHID)<br/>(a) to (c) : The Government of West Bengal had sent a proposal for<br/>establishment of a Circuit Bench of the Calcutta High Court at Jalpaiguri. records.subject: Demand to expedite the establishment of Indian Defence University.
records.SM_Text:
Shri Sukhendu Sekhar Ray: Indian National Defence University (INDU) had been proposed to be established by the Government as a World Class Premier autonomous ?Institution of National Importance? for developing and propagating higher education in Armed Forces, Para Military Forces, Central Armed Police Force, Civil Servants and Military and Civil officers from Friendly Foreign Countries. In May, 2013, foundation stone was laid for setting up Indian National Defence University on 202 acres of land at Binola in Haryana and compensation was paid to land owners. Details of the foundation stone laying ceremony were widely publicized in media. A draft Bill regarding establishment of Indian National Defence University was published online in August 5, 2016 for public consideration. However, the Bill was further revised in December 2017 and the project was renamed to the Indian Defence University. The approval of the cabinet relating to the Bill is reportedly still awaited. I therefore urge upon the Government to expedite the process of legislation in national interest, considering the fact that this will be the first Defence University in the country.

(ENDS)

records.subject: REPATRIATION OF SMUGGLED STOLEN INDIAN ANQUITIES FROM FOREIGN COUNTRIES
records.SM_Text:
Shri Sukhendu Sekhar Ray: As per reports published in indianculture.gov.in and various news reports published in national dailies till recently, it appears that many Indian antiquities stolen from different temples and museums across the country were smuggled out from time to time found to be stored in various museums and private galleries/auction centers in foreign countries. However, some of those antiquities started being repatriated to India since past few decades due to bilateral investigations and diplomatic initiatives taken by India and the concerned countries. The Metropolitan Museum of New York alone returned hundreds of such stolen Indian antiquities in 2015-2016. Again in July, 2023, US Metropolitan Museum returned 105 trafficked Indian artifacts. Out of the latest repatriated antiquities, a few date back to 1st century BC to 16th CE and originated from UP, West Bengal, Bihar, South India and other parts of the country. It is not known as to where the repatriated hundreds of antiquities are presently stored in India. I would request the Government to inform about the exact number of antiquities recovered from foreign countries, their places of origin and present places of storage. I would also urge upon the Government to return the recovered antiquities originated from Chandraketugarh and other archaeological sites of West Bengal to the State Archaeological Museum or Indian Museum in Kolkata so that the people of Bengal can have a sight of those invaluable artifacts and feel the pride of the past glories and rich histories of the concerned places.

(Ends)

records.subject: Demand for restoration of public immigration service at Mahadipur Malda District of West Bengal.
records.SM_Text:
SHRI SUKHENDU SEKHAR RAY (West Bengal): Sir, public immigration service at Mahadipur Immigration Check Post in Malda District of West Bengal for movement of common citizens, such as tourists, patients, exporters and importers of both India and Bangladesh was suspended in the wake of Covid-19 pandemic. While many other International Immigration Check Post bordering Bangladesh have since been opened for movement of immigrants following phenomenal improvement of Covid situation, the Immigration Check Post in Mahadipur in Malda District of West Bengal has not yet resumed the Immigration services. I would therefore, urge upon the Government to initiate appropriate steps so that the severe constraints being confronted by the local immigrants are removed and there is resumption of pre-Covid immigration services at Mahadipur Immigration Check Post without any further loss of time.

(Ends)

records.subject: Demand to curb the unfair practice of import of jute sacking bags as hessian fabric through Nepal.
records.SM_Text:
SHRI SUKHENDU SEKHAR RAY (West Bengal): Sir, as per the Notification No.01/2017-Customs (ADD) of the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, as amended from time to time, imposition of definitive anti-dumping duty on imports of jute yarn/twine, hessian fabric and jute sacking bags originating in or exported from Nepal and imported into India has been recommended.? As per the said notification, ADD on hessian fabric is either nil or lower than ADD on sacking bags. To circumvent the actual levy, a section of traders in Nepal are reportedly resorting to the unfair practice of passing off jute sacking bags as hessian fabric, as a result of which our domestic jute industry is not only suffering but also our Government is losing huge revenue on account of legitimate duty.

would, therefore, urge upon the hon. Finance Minister to have the matter inquired into for appropriate remedial measure. Thank you.

(Ends)
